page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the t2d server family. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with both read and write large-block tests scoring in the bottom 25%, and PassMark memory benchmarks ranking in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, while multi-threaded decompression is poor.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but low overall core and memory count, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that require predictable CPU performance without the overhead of larger instances. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale parallel processing due to its constrained memory bandwidth and multi-core limitations.
